title: Sparse Adaptation for In-Context Learning on Data Streams
abstract: arXiv:2611.33325v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) generates massive data streams, making edge computing essential for low-latency applications and 5G networks. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) enable adaptation through in-context examples rather than parameter updates, but evolving streams challenge context relevance and computational efficiency. This work introduces SAIL, a framework for sparse adaptation of TFMs that reuses the model's key--value cache between adaptation events. SAIL reconstructs its support set only when drifts in stream structure indicate potential context inadequacy, while the structural representation itself is updated by changes in predictive performance. SAIL combines prequential error monitoring with online, class-specific micro-clustering to detect changes in cluster mass, class separability, and feature-space coverage. translated_title: 数据流上上下文学习的稀疏自适应
translated_abstract: 物联网（IoT）产生了海量数据流，使得边缘计算对于低延迟应用和5G网络至关重要。表格基础模型（TFMs）能够通过上下文示例而非参数更新来实现适应，但不断演变的数据流对上下文的相关性和计算效率提出了挑战。本工作提出了SAIL，一个用于TFMs稀疏适应的框架，它在各次适应事件之间重用模型的键值缓存。SAIL仅在数据流结构出现漂移、表明当前上下文可能不足以应对时，才重建其支持集，而其结构表示本身则通过预测性能的变化进行更新。SAIL将预序误差监测与在线的、面向类别的微聚类相结合，以检测聚类质量、类别可分离性和特征空间覆盖范围的变化。在进行适应时，上下文预算按类别质量成比例分配，并将最近更新的微……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出SAIL框架，通过重用键值缓存、结合漂移检测与在线微聚类的稀疏适应机制，使表格基础模型能够在动态演变的物联网数据流上高效进行上下文学习。
